idiom_name: @JvmInline value class over Long minor units with a currency type parameter
implementation_notes: Kotlin's inline value classes give the wrapper for free: an @JvmInline value class over a Long count of minor units - with the currency as a type parameter or an enum - is erased to its underlying value at runtime while the compiler still refuses to mix it with plain Longs or with another currency, so the classic Money class becomes a zero-allocation alias with operator functions. Where scale must exceed the minor unit, the practical variant is an immutable data class over java.math.BigDecimal with copy-on-operation semantics and setScale(scale, RoundingMode.HALF_EVEN) at settlement, since BigDecimal is the JVM primitive Kotlin inherits. Reach for JSR 354 through Moneta and the money-kotlin extension functions when ISO currency metadata, rounding objects and FX conversion should come off the shelf rather than be re-derived.
pitfalls: Value classes are boxed when used generically, nullably or as array elements, so the zero-allocation claim holds only in direct use.
java.math.BigDecimal exists only on the JVM; Kotlin Multiplatform needs a pure-Kotlin decimal or scaled integers.
JSR 354 providers are discovered as runtime singletons, so tests must bootstrap javax.money rather than assume a container.

variants.name: JSR 354 via Moneta with the money-kotlin extensions
variants.implementation_notes: On the JVM, Kotlin can use the Java money standard directly: javax.money defines MonetaryAmount and CurrencyUnit, Moneta implements them, and the money-kotlin extensions add operator functions, builders and a currency-scoped ofCurrency, so prices read as 200.ofCurrency("EUR") instead of a builder chain. Pick this when ISO metadata, provider-based rounding and exchange rates matter more than a dependency-free domain type; the value-class route stays preferable for small services that only need one currency or a fixed set.
variants.code_sketch:
val price: MonetaryAmount = 12.99.ofCurrency<FastMoney>("USD")  // money-kotlin
val tax = price * 0.21                                          // MonetaryOperator
val total = price + tax                                         // same currency required
pitfalls: Moneta pulls a provider and a service loader into the classpath, which is heavy for a library that only formats amounts.
Money and FastMoney from Moneta are unequal for the same amount and currency, so the implementation type leaks into equality.
